orchestrator_findings.finding: The Traefik block was written against a premise the cluster does not hold. Read from the cluster: namespace k3s-stg-ninjasre, ingress `console`, class traefik-prod, and it routes exactly two paths — /webhooks to `app` and / to `web`. There is no /v1 path on the ingress at all, so /v1/events/stream never traverses Traefik as itself: the browser reaches the Next.js route console/src/app/api/events/route.ts on `web`, which proxies to the gateway inside the cluster. The per-run stream the block says to mirror has the same shape (console/src/app/api/stream/[runId]/route.ts) and carries no Traefik configuration of its own — the ingress has no annotations.
orchestrator_findings.second_finding: Traefik CRDs are not installed on this cluster (`middlewares.traefik.io` is not a resource type), so the Middleware/label form the block proposes cannot be applied as written.
orchestrator_findings.why_it_probably_needs_nothing: traefik:v3.6.17 runs with no responding/forwarding timeout overrides, so defaults apply: flushInterval 100ms (no response buffering), writeTimeout 0 (unbounded), and idleTimeout governs idle keep-alive connections rather than an active streaming response — which a 15s keep-alive frame would keep non-idle regardless. The 10-minute hold SC-004 requires is within defaults.
orchestrator_findings.how_it_gets_settled: T062's `curl -N` 10-minute hold against https://stg-ninjasre.lan.kyo.ninja measures it end to end. Only if that fails does a Traefik change have a subject; if it passes, T061 closes as 'no change required, and here is the measurement', not as applied.
